text:
B: Alright mate, how's it going?
A: Alright. Yeah, fine.
B: Zain, Bolton. You're the gym lad, aren't you? From the picture, the Gymshark top.
A: Callum. Stockton. Yeah, I go a fair bit.
B: Same, three times a week, weights. What you on?
A: Four mornings, before lectures. Trying to get a hundred and forty on deadlift.
B: A hundred and forty? Fair play. I'm nowhere near. I've been doing padel lately as well, mate from work dragged me along. Proper addictive. You ever tried it?
A: No. Not really my thing.
B: Fair enough. What you studying?
A: Civil engineering. Final year. Teesside.
B: Oh nice, I love all that. I'm a sparky, but I watch loads of stuff on YouTube about old mills getting converted. There's one in Bolton they've done flats in, kept all the brick and the iron columns. Proper nice.
A: Yeah, the cast iron ones are interesting. You've got to check them before you put load on, half of them weren't designed for what people want now.
B: See, that's the stuff I want to know. What you doing your dissertation on?
A: Drainage. New housing estates.
B: Drainage. Right.
A: It's more interesting than it sounds.
B: Go on then, sell it me.
A: Every new estate's adding roofs and tarmac, so the rain can't soak in. It all goes in the pipes at once and floods somewhere downstream. So you design it to hold back, ponds, swales, permeable paving, and let it out slowly. If you get it wrong, people's houses flood. If you get it right, nobody notices. That's it really.
B: Nah, that's mint, that. The nobody-notices bit. Same with wiring. Do a good job and no one thinks about you again.
A: Yeah. Pretty much.
B: You go to the football? I'm Wanderers.
A: Boro. Watch most of it on telly with my stepdad. Go to the Riverside a few times a season.
B: Same with me and my cousins. We've played yous a few times in pre-season and that. What d'you reckon to your manager?
A: Should've gone in October, to be honest.
B: Ha, blunt. I like it. Ours, I'd give him till the summer. You play at all?
A: Used to. Sunday league. Stopped.
B: How come?
A: Didn't like the lads' side of it. All the banter and that.
B: Ah, fair. Our five-a-side's bad for that, to be fair. There's one lad never passes and we never stop giving him stick. He deserves it, mind.
A: Probably.
B: What you doing after uni, then? Staying up there?
A: Yeah. Consultancy in the North East. Get chartered. Save for a house.
B: Sound. I'm going on my own, two years. Van, my name on the side, EV chargers and solar. That's where the money is.
A: You'll need someone good on the paperwork for that.
B: Ha, you're the second person to say that today. I'm on it, mate. Think the timer's about to go.
A: Yeah. Good luck with it.
